# Verification record 2026-10-10.2

<!-- Generated by `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs render` from 2026-10-10.2.json; do not edit. -->

**Verification is evidence, not a support guarantee.** This record is the result of one full nightly run of the [compatibility matrix](../cells/COMPATIBILITY.md) at commit `83aa8a8c51db80e6c1297b5a895fdcbbd4134994`, with each render backend checked separately. The machine-readable record is [2026-10-10.2.json](2026-10-10.2.json); `verifiedRanges` in [seed.json](../seed.json) is derived from the records (`node design/compatibility/verification.mjs ranges`), and `validate.mjs` checks that they agree.

**Rendering: software (GPU profile `software`).** Software rendering: no GPU took part. WebGL ran on ANGLE over SwiftShader and WebGPU on Dawn over SwiftShader's Vulkan device, a fallback adapter (isFallbackAdapter true). It counts as verification; a run on a real GPU (run-cells.mjs --gpu hardware) can be added later as extra evidence.

Rule: A tuple (React adapter, exact React, Pixi adapter, exact pixi.js) is verified on a render backend when its cell passed on that backend in this record (every command, every conformance scenario and the render check) and every boundary probe and every negative case of this record behaved as expected. A run on the expected-blank-render list (adapterMatrix.expectedBlankRender) that failed exactly as listed is not a failure, but verifies nothing. Each tuple lists every backend it is verified on; backends are never inferred from each other.

## Run

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build --force`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs pack --out <work>/tarballs`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs run --tier nightly --patches all --cell <a third of the cells> --no-cache --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs   (three shards in parallel)`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs probes --tier nightly --work <work>`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs run --negative --no-cache --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs`
- `node design/compatibility/cells/run-cells.mjs data --work <work> --tarballs <work>/tarballs`
- `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs build --work <work> --date 2026-10-10 --sequence 2 --commit 83aa8a8c51db80e6c1297b5a895fdcbbd4134994 --extra <notes>`

- Tier: nightly with `--patches all` (297 cells: every React adapter, React 18.0 to 19.3, at its minimum and latest audited patch x the newest audited patch of every Pixi 8 minor and pixi.js 7.2.0, 7.2.4, 7.3.0, 7.3.3, 7.4.2 and 7.4.3), a superset of the scheduled nightly tier's 216 cells. Render backends: WebGL and WebGPU (`adapterMatrix.tiers.nightly.renderers`); Pixi 7 cells WebGL only.
- Second full record of this machine and software profile on 2026-10-10 (`--sequence 2`): it supersedes the first 2026-10-10 record, whose 184 cells ran before the React 18 minors became packages (react-18.0 to react-18.3, the old react-18 renamed react-18.3) and before the Pixi 7 adapter covered 7.2 and 7.3. Only the newest record of a machine and GPU profile counts, so verifiedRanges derive from this record (plus other machines' records).
- Commit 83aa8a8 on claude/react18-minors-pixi7-widen. Fresh: a new work directory, packages rebuilt with `pnpm build --force`, tarballs packed from that build, `--no-cache` (no verdict reused), CI=true. The npm download cache was shared (registry tarballs are integrity-checked).
- Three cell shards ran in parallel on 4 vCPUs with the probes (cells 16:24 to 17:23 UTC, 59 minutes; about 35 s per cell per shard), then the negative cases and the data-only probes. No test timed out and no failure was retried.
- Cells with React 18.0.0, 18.1.0 and 18.2.0 ran with harness/test/lend-act.ts, which lends React the act of react-dom/test-utils (React exports act from 18.3.0 on); the adapters and every check are unchanged. Pixi 7.2 cells compiled the Pixi 7 type consumer without the pixi8-names-rejected assertions (adapterMatrix typeAssertions, from 7.3.0), recorded in each cell.json.
- Commits after this one change documentation, generated tables, the verification tooling and comments only; `node design/compatibility/verification.mjs compare --record 2026-10-10.2 --tarballs <fresh pack>` shows whether a later commit packs the same code (Markdown and build logs aside).

## Findings

- WebGL: all 297 cells passed (every command, every conformance scenario, the render check), including every React 18 minor package (18.0.0, 18.1.0, 18.2.0, 18.3.1) and pixi.js 7.2.0, 7.2.4, 7.3.0 and 7.3.3 with every React adapter.
- WebGPU: 143 of 231 Pixi 8 cells passed and are verified on WebGPU: pixi.js 8.10.2 to 8.22.0 with every React adapter and patch. The other 88 are every React adapter and patch (11 each) on pixi.js 8.2.6, 8.3.4, 8.4.1, 8.5.2, 8.6.6, 8.7.3, 8.8.1 and 8.9.2: every conformance scenario passed and the canvas stayed blank exactly as adapterMatrix.expectedBlankRender lists: expected blank render, unverified.
- The blank render is an upstream pixi.js bug before 8.10 (pixijs/pixijs#11389, fixed by #11417 in 8.10.0): the WebGPU batch is sized from WebGL's 32 texture units while the device allows 16 sampled textures per stage, so the pipeline is invalid. It hits any device with that mismatch, not only software rendering; the partial hardware record 2026-10-10-macos-26-apple-m5-max renders 8.2.6 to 8.9.2 on WebGPU (WebGL reports 16 units there).
- React 18.0, 18.1 and 18.2 behave like 18.3: the four reconcilers (0.27.0, 0.28.0, 0.29.0, 0.29.2) take the same host config, every scenario passed on both backends, and the React 18.0 adapter beside React 18.3.1 is rejected at composition, naming react-18.3 (negative case).
- Rendering was software throughout (no GPU in the machine): WebGL on ANGLE/SwiftShader, WebGPU on SwiftShader's fallback adapter. Owner ruling: software rendering counts as verification; real-GPU records add evidence.
- Boundary probes: 51 of 51 passed (pixi-8.5.0 by failing exactly as the audit recorded; no API or type drift), including the new react-18.0.0, 18.1.0, 18.2.0 and pixi-7.2.0, 7.2.4, 7.3.0, 7.3.3 tuples. Incompatible pairs: 7 of 7 rejected as expected.

## Data only, not verified

**Data only, not verified: these results are never verification, never enter verifiedRanges and never change a peer range.**

Data-only probes (issue 17). Each probe installs the packed adapters beside a React or pixi.js the adapter does not declare, ignoring peers, and records what every cell command does. The adapters' environment checks are bypassed in the conformance run only (cell.json dataOnly.bypassEnvironmentCheck), so the suite shows what would happen past them. Results are data, never verification: nothing here enters verifiedRanges or changes a peer range.

### pixi7-earlier-releases

The Pixi 7 adapter on pixi.js releases outside its peer range: the highest patch of 7.0 and 7.1 (below the 7.2.0 floor), and the excluded 7.4.0 (7.4.1 was never published to npm). Pixi 7.2 and 7.3, and React 18.0 to 18.2, were data-only probes until they became matrix cells (React 18 per-minor packages, the Pixi 7 range widened to 7.2).

- pixi.js 7.4.1: not run, absent from the npm registry's version list and time map: there is nothing to install.

### Data-only findings

- pixi.js 7.4.0: the adapter's entry fails to import in plain Node ('Worker is not defined', a pixi.js 7.4.0 module-scope dependency on a browser global); in Chromium, past checkEnvironment(), the whole suite passes with React 18.3.1 and 19.3.0; types pass. It stays excluded from the peer range.
- pixi.js 7.1.4 and 7.0.5: the adapter cannot load. pixi.js 7.1 does not export HTMLText, and 7.0 does not export the filters or HTMLText from its root, which the adapter's entry imports by name: Node import and the browser build fail, so no conformance scenario ran. Types also fail.
- pixi.js 7.4.1 was never published to npm, so nothing ran for it.
- React 18.0 to 18.2 and pixi.js 7.2 and 7.3, data-only probes in the first 2026-10-10 record, are matrix cells in this one.
